clue.text: Fruit and nut almost halved deficiency disease reportedly

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: a nut is a crank, an eccentric person

halved means only the first half of the disease's name is kept

parts.note: beriberi is a disease caused by lack of vitamin B1

explanation.surface: A nutty person, half-crazed, apparently suffering from a vitamin-deficiency illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CRANK to CRAN; 'halved' takes BERI from BERIBERI, and 'reportedly' turns that into the fruit word it sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranberry is a tart red fruit, often made into a sauce or juice.

clue.text: What Batman wears to run and leap about

parts.note: Batman wears a cape

parts.note: a carouser is a noisy reveller
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rouses others is one who wakes them up.

clue.text: Money from short book, second hand?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a second-hand book has already been read

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'second hand' is a loose cryptic hint: most used books have been read.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, like 'dough'.

clue.text: He's not the first with a couple of bits of rude news to upset virgin

parts.words: a couple of bits of rude
parts.note: the first two letters of the word rude
news treated as more than one new, N for new twice

explanation.walkthrough: The setter has confirmed 'news' means two news, N plus N, rather than its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up finishes second, behind the winner.

clue.text: Lots of yuck followed by short police enquiry into Spanish daggers

short means the word is cut back by one letter

parts.note: a police enquiry is a case

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish daggers' look like weapons but are the plant: Spanish dagger is a common name for a kind of yucca.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish dagger is a popular name for certain spiky-leaved yucca plants.

clue.text: Oddly statue by church is brass

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word statue

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like the metal of the statue, but here it means cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for impudence or nerve, as in 'the brass neck' or 'none of your lip'.

clue.text: Maybe rustling gang sets ranch in a spin

explanation.definitionFit: Rustlers steal livestock, so a rustling gang would be cattle snatchers.

clue.text: Tunic ornament bears heraldic beast

indicators.note: bears means the phrase carries the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A decoration on a tunic shows a creature from a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a mythical horned horse common in heraldry.

clue.text: All who might deserve favours if good when embracing daughter?

parts.words: who might deserve favours if good
parts.note: from the music mnemonic Every Good Boy Deserves Favour, with good dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The mnemonic for treble-clef lines is Every Good Boy Deserves Favour; the clue's 'if good' points there.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody means all people collectively.

clue.text: Proactive after scrapping first part of play in show

clue.text: A sort of trance in ecstasy — this is peachy!

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, so it is literally peachy.

clue.text: What's left of uniform kept in lodge

indicators.note: kept in means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to lodge somewhere is to reside there
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: A residue is the remainder or leftover part after something has gone.

clue.text: Fish creating havoc? Yes/No

indicators.note: creating suggests the letters are worked up into something new

clue.text: Outdoor food from pub — because all traces of 24 6Ac gone

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: gone means the named letters are removed from the word because
all traces of here means the initial letter of each of the two answers referred to

parts.note: the answer to 24 down
the answer to 6 across

explanation.surface: Pub grub served outside, because there is no apple sauce left.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 6Ac' points to the answers APPLE and SAUCE; their traces are their opening letters A and S, which come out of BECAUSE to leave BECUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a meal grilled and eaten outdoors.

clue.text: Blown up explosive device when sound of timer's stopped?

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device
as can mean when

clue.text: Like an eel, one cooked with Viv, say?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared in a new form

explanation.definitionFit: Eels are slippery, so moving like an eel is dodging slyly.

clue.text: Without any fat to shed

parts.note: meat without any fat is lean

explanation.surface: An instruction to lose weight: with no fat left at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb meaning lose, but it is a noun: a small hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a small shed built against an existing wall.

clue.text: Mafioso's unease when in Germany

indicators.note: when in means placed inside

parts.note: angst is anxiety or unease

explanation.definitionFit: A mafioso is a member of the Mafia, a gang criminal.

clue.text: Note structure's snapped off in accident

clue.text: Cork perhaps from sun hat

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' may suggest the Irish city, but it is the bottle seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork is one kind of bottle stopper.

clue.text: How one thing leads to another! - (if it gave us a turn it would be incidentally)

definitions.text: How one thing leads to another!

indicators.text: if it gave us a turn it would be
indicators.note: the answer, with its letters u and s turned round, would be the word meaning incidentally

parts.note: casually means incidentally, in passing

explanation.surface: A remark on cause and effect, with an aside about turning us round.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket works backwards: swap the order of U and S in the answer and you get CASUALLY, meaning incidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Things linked causally are related as cause and effect, each producing the next.

clue.text: Source of wool when originally treated for carpet

parts.note: a lamb is a source of wool
as can mean when

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Wool for a carpet, treated at its source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' looks like a rug, but is the verb: to scold severely.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone, in British usage, is to reprimand them harshly.

clue.text: Where opening of bible is translated — from this?

definitions.text: Where opening of bible is translated — from this?

indicators.note: is translated means the letters are turned into another form
opening of means the first letter of the word bible

explanation.surface: A question asking which language the Bible was first translated from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament was written mostly in Hebrew, so translations begin from that language.

clue.text: Poison — it's found in an ice cream

the word it, with 's standing for 'is'

clue.text: Pound each way put on gee-gee? Half that according to rule book

clue.text: Program is axed for IT company

clue.text: Turner's rubbish, getting nothing right

O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but here is anything that turns.

clue.text: All but leader in retrospect shot — highly hush-hush

all but leader means the word retrospect loses its opening letter
